applied.action: Removed the duplicated H2 glued to the end of the Hardware Reality paragraph ('...[[readmemd]].## Training Topologies'), leaving a single '## Training Topologies' on its own line. The duplicate heading is gone; the H2 count is unchanged at 8.

Opening thesis rewritten to match the body's arithmetic: 'the all-reduce is slower than the model assumes once the right column is read' (numerator grows 1.48x) and 'the step is far longer ... once attention is counted', with 'the second correction dominates — the ratio falls 5.4x'. Removed the false 'they nearly cancel' causal story and its 'which is why the conclusion looks sound' clause.

6.6% replaced by an explicit T4 range wherever it is load-bearing: thesis now reads '5.3–7.1% at Gen2 x4 ... 11.4% at Gen1 x4, 1.5% at Gen2 x16 (T4)'; the derivation paragraph states the 6.6% is 'a T4 extrapolation, not a measurement' scaling a three-card Gen2 x16 receipt, gives the report's own calibrated algbw band (5.3–6.1%) and busbw row (7.1%), and adds the unquantified N=5 alignment penalty. Verdict (a) now says 'single-digit percent at Gen2 x4'; the claim table and the topology table carry the range. Added the algbw-only reproducibility of the 36% ('under the busbw reading it is 54–58% at the plan's denominator').

EP exclusion restated as absence-of-evidence rather than evidence-of-absence: 'the corpus holds no evidence of a training-grade EP implementation for a no-P2P, no-NVLink, no-RDMA fabric — the closest are VarioPath ... and ThunderEP ... Both are systems projects to port, not hardware impossibilities.'

'only one is physically possible' -> 'only one is consistent with the best measured efficiency'. Added the 72%-confidence qualifier, the 494M/140k tok/s datapoint that weakly favours algbw, the P2P-is-a-driver-configuration scenario in which algbw becomes plausible and the overhead doubles, and the pre-flight instruction to establish P2P with cuMemcpyPeer rather than cudaDeviceCanAccessPeer.

Freeze-vs-replicate distinction added: 'Freezing removes the gradient collective; replicating the table removes the forward gather collective, and the design needs both', with the frozen-but-sharded alternative at ~4.9 GB/card and the forward all-to-all at one-fifth the volume.

TP restated as feasible-but-dominated: table cell 'Ruled out on placement' -> 'Feasible, dominated'; the TP paragraph now says 'TP is dominated rather than ruled out', cites on-optimizing-the-communication-of-model-parallelism for overlap and efficient-training-on-multiple-consumer-gpus-with for TP overtaking DP above ~20B on PCIe; Verdict (b) says 'True for EP; for TP the fabric does not rule it out so much as make it lose'.

The 11x internal inconsistency is now stated explicitly in 'The table is 24 GB, not 12 GB': the 24.58 GB figure holds only on the paper's 3M entries per layer, and the repo's §3 '33M entries per grafted layer' implies 135 GB/layer and 270 GB for two, which fits neither 64 GB nor the 320 GB aggregate. Verdict (c) now carries the same condition ('only on the paper's 3M entries per layer; on the repo's §3 figure of 33M the table is 270 GB and the claim is false'). The secondary rho=0 / LongCat-50%-cap caveat was not added (length cap).

Added the 'why the port is hard' mechanism paragraph after the five-row stack table: Hopper wgmma.mma_async vs Ampere mma.sync with TileLang's 1.81x fallback (possible-but-slow, not impossible); StreamIndex at 8% of H200 BF16 peak against TileLang's 40%, so even a 64x FLOP cut does not yield a usable training kernel; HISA's 1.6 ms Sparse MLA vs 5.6 ms indexer at 64K on A100; and the V4.1-Flash layer mix (2 SWA + 4 Full + 4 Reindex + 30 Reuse) that makes attention density, not the 16,384 cap, the right quantity.

Added a sequenced program to the Verdict after the four premise checks: GQA check as a free gate that can drop the sparse arm before kernel work; the architecture comparison moved to 8K on a four-point ladder (50M/125M/250M/500M x 2 architectures) trained to ~1/3 of budget with the first 10% of checkpoints discarded, fitting L(C) and comparing exponents (~12–35 days); CSA2/NSA alone at 32k with a phase-stratified metric; and the 100B-per-arm wall-clock (43–58 days per arm, 215–290 for five) that rules out matching the literature.

Data-pipeline verdict inverted: 'The data pipeline is the part of the plan that is wrong.' The paragraph now states that the repo's default (random interleaving with document-boundary masking off) is MIXChunk, cites the measured INTRADoc advantage (0.762 PPL at 2K, 0.986 at 8K), the code-specific damage (−1.3 / −2.0 PPL on GitHub), that code is 15% of the mix, that cu_seqlens is already stored so the fix is a kernel flag, and its measured 4.0% step-time cost. Removed the false 'Packing ... is standard and not cosmetic' claim.

bf16_compress_hook now has a verdict: ~3% of step time at the corrected window (1.85 s saved against 56.3 s), ~18% only under the plan's own 36% premise; the measured A6000 analogue (+33%) corresponds to a 131% overhead regime; and the cluster consensus that compression pays more, not less, on slow fabrics (AGoQ 3.7x at 10 Gbps vs 3.4x at 200 Gbps; CERAR −17.3% on PCIe vs 33% slower on NVLink). Framed as insurance against the Gen1-x4 and short-context cases, not a lever at 32k.

Added the 5-rank ring-pathology paragraph after the busbw derivation: Tartan's 'One should avoid adopting 5 GPUs in their application setup' and the NCCL maintainer's offset-alignment explanation with the 16x5-byte padding remedy. States that every overhead figure is a floor and that bucket padding belongs in the pre-flight.

Added the batch-shape paragraph to the Verdict: 1M tokens is ~17x below the measured CBS at plateau (~16.8M tokens) but CBS is near zero at initialisation, so a fixed 1M batch from step 0 is far above it; the measured consequence (fixed 4,096-document batch ends worse than the small-batch control despite 75% fewer steps; batch-size warmup beats that control by 0.0166 loss with 43% fewer steps); and that the linear LR-scaling rule is an SGD-on-vision result.

ECC sentence replaced with the temporal resolution: off/N/A through cmpunlocker v0.4, v0.5 (2026-10-06) reports N/A -> Enabled at ≤0.3% integration-level cost with integration-level-only verification; amoghmunikote lists Working while bayley, dl4rce and the 170th Street spec sheet say not restored. Converted to a two-part pre-flight: enable ECC, deploy the five-minute counter snapshot, and run memtest_vulkan over the full 64 GB rather than the 8 GiB region.

Sequence parallelism added as the sixth topology in the enumeration (Ulysses all-to-all on the head dimension, Ring Attention P2P ring passes, the standard alternative to activation checkpointing at 32k), with an SP=5 row in the corrected-comparison table (62.9 GB/GPU/step, ~1.4x, ruled out on availability) and a matching sentence in the table's summary paragraph. 'Five ways' -> 'Six ways'.

Stated the unstated precision premise: 2.0 GB is 2 bytes/param and is only reachable with bf16_compress_hook registered; under standard AMP the buckets stay fp32 (4.0 GB) and the overhead doubles; with pure-bf16 parameters the hook is a no-op cast. Cited the measured PCIe-only result (2.06x -> 2.65x at 124M, 1.91x -> 2.72x at 355M). Added a 2M-token row to the overhead table (112.6 s compute, 4.0 s all-reduce, 3.5%; 7.1% with fp32 buckets) and a sentence stating the invariance claim holds at both batch sizes.

Added both named mechanisms to the payoff subsection: top-k is non-differentiable, so the indexer is trained by clipped-log KL distillation against the main attention distribution rather than end-to-end, adding a second score-tensor forward+backward and a separate loss term per step; and the indexer's cost is additive and measured at 3.5x the kernel it feeds (HISA 5.6 ms vs 1.6 ms), so the −20% to −30% payoff is not net of it.

Added the missing TP row to the claim-by-claim verdict table: 'TP ruled out at ~70x | ~70x | ~2.8x arithmetic (126 GB/GPU/step, 156 s); no training-grade TP path on a no-P2P link | T4/T3 | Wrong by ~25x; dominated, not excluded'.
